name: Low taper fade

lead: A low taper fade is a men's cut in which the sides and back are clipped short and graduated, starting low near the ears and nape, with more length left on top.

Its appearance payoff is a clean outline that makes the head and jaw look tidier and the hair on top look fuller by contrast. It belongs to the long family of short back and sides cuts that Wikipedia traces to Roman legionaries.

paras: A barber uses clippers with graded guards, lifting them away as they move upward so the length blends. People bring photos and name the guard lengths. Touch-ups every few weeks keep the edge sharp.
Few risks beyond razor irritation or a cut that comes out shorter than intended. It reveals scalp, scars or head shape that longer hair would cover.

angle.text: The cut changes how the head and jaw are framed: shorter sides emphasise facial structure, while a low fade keeps a subtle, natural transition.

lead: The low taper fade is a clipper haircut in which hair is graduated from very short at the bottom to longer above, with the fade line sitting low around the ears and neckline. Wikipedia's article on hairstyles lists the short taper cut as a form of fade, in which a coarse clipper is gradually lifted away so the length blends smoothly [1].
It descends from the short back and sides, which Wikipedia dates to Roman legionaries and which returned in the Renaissance and the Regency era, and was the norm for professional men by 1910 [1].
No published study has examined the cut itself.

paras: Wikipedia describes short tapers as using fine clippers at the sideburns and extending about an inch above the ear, with sideburns kept short. The taper can pair with styles such as ivy league, high and tight or flat top [1].

The short back and sides dates back to Roman legionaries, was revived in the Renaissance and the Regency period (about 1810 to 1830), and was the standard for professional men by 1910. The post-war businessman cut was the office standard until the late 1960s or early 1970s [1].

timeline.event: Short back and sides is the norm for professional men [1].
